{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go",
      "line": 50,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Async legacy writes use the request-scoped context and will be canceled immediately",
      "body": "In Create (lines 50-56), Delete (108-113), Update (134-140), and DeleteCollection (161-166), the goroutine creates a timeout context from the request context (ctx). When the HTTP handler returns, its context is typically canceled. The goroutine's legacy write then inherits this canceled context and is aborted before completing. This defeats the purpose of asynchronous fallback writes: the legacy store will almost never receive the write. The code should use a context detached from the request (e.g., context.Background() with timeout) while preserving any necessary values (like authentication)."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go",
      "line": 139,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Legacy update uses the original objInfo instead of the object updated in unified storage",
      "body": "In Update, after d.Storage.Update succeeds, the goroutine calls d.Legacy.Update with the same objInfo that was passed to the unified storage call. The previous implementation used an updateWrapper to reuse the already computed updated object. Without it, Legacy.Update will invoke objInfo.UpdatedObject against the legacy store's own old object, which may differ (e.g., missing new fields, different resourceVersion). This can cause the legacy write to produce a different object or fail validation, breaking the dual-write guarantee. The code should pass a wrapper or the object returned by Storage.Update to ensure both stores persist the same data."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go",
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Multiple metrics are recorded under the wrong name or store",
      "body": "Several metric calls are incorrect: in Create error path (line 45) records legacy duration instead of storage; in Update error path (line 129) records legacy duration instead of storage; in Delete success path (line 106) passes the resource name as the 'kind' label instead of options.Kind; in DeleteCollection goroutine (line 166) records storage duration for the legacy operation instead of legacy duration. These errors cause Prometheus metrics to be mislabeled or attributed to the wrong store, leading to incorrect monitoring and alerting. All timing and label arguments must be corrected to reflect the actual operation being measured."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go",
      "line": 97,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Delete uses the base logger instead of the request-scoped logger",
      "body": "In Delete, ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) is used, discarding the enriched log variable (log) that includes name, kind, and method fields. Consequently, subsequent logs in the Delete method (including errors from Storage.Delete) will lack these contextual fields, making debugging harder. It should be ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, log)."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go",
      "line": 55,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Legacy Create receives the original input object, not the object persisted in unified storage",
      "body": "In Create, the goroutine passes `obj` (the original input) to Legacy.Create, ignoring the `created` object returned by Storage.Create. Unified storage typically applies defaulting, assigns UID, resourceVersion, and creationTimestamp. The legacy store will therefore receive an object missing these modifications, leading to data inconsistency between the two stores. The code should pass `created` (or a sanitized copy) to the legacy write to ensure both stores reflect the same final state."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode1_test.go",
      "line": 138,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Removal of local prometheus registry causes duplicate metric registration panic",
      "body": "The diff removes `p := prometheus.NewRegistry()` from TestMode1_Get, causing it to use the package-level global `p` (var p = prometheus.NewRegistry()). If NewDualWriter registers metrics on the provided registry (as dualWriterMetrics likely does using promauto), then the first test that uses the global registry (e.g., TestMode1_Create) will register metrics, and any subsequent test using the same global registry will panic with duplicate metric registration. This will break the entire test package. Each test should create and use its own fresh prometheus registry, or the global registry must be reset between tests."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go",
      "line": 31,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Tests for asynchronous legacy writes do not wait for completion and ignore mock expectations",
      "body": "Multiple tests (e.g., TestMode3_Create, TestMode3_Delete, TestMode3_Update) set up legacy mock expectations but never call m.AssertExpectations() and do not wait for the goroutine to finish. The test may pass even if the legacy write is never called or fails, and the mock call may occur after the test completes, causing race conditions or panics if the legacy method is not stubbed. This prevents any verification of the asynchronous dual-write behavior and can lead to flaky or silently failing tests. The tests must synchronize with the goroutine (e.g., using a WaitGroup or a done channel) and assert expectations before finishing."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go",
      "line": 141,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Integration tests for mode 3 may be flaky due to asynchronous legacy writes",
      "body": "The added subtests for mode 3 (file and unified storage) run the same doPlaylistTests which immediately checks legacy API results after k8s API operations. Since mode 3 writes to legacy asynchronously, there is no guarantee that the legacy write has completed before the test queries the legacy endpoint. This can cause intermittent failures (e.g., legacy list missing the just-created playlist). The test needs a synchronization mechanism or a polling wait to ensure the async write has propagated before asserting on the legacy API."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Async legacy writes use the request-scoped context and will be canceled immediately
findings.body: In Create (lines 50-56), Delete (108-113), Update (134-140), and DeleteCollection (161-166), the goroutine creates a timeout context from the request context (ctx). When the HTTP handler returns, its context is typically canceled. The goroutine's legacy write then inherits this canceled context and is aborted before completing. This defeats the purpose of asynchronous fallback writes: the legacy store will almost never receive the write. The code should use a context detached from the request (e.g., context.Background() with timeout) while preserving any necessary values (like authentication).

findings.title: Legacy update uses the original objInfo instead of the object updated in unified storage
findings.body: In Update, after d.Storage.Update succeeds, the goroutine calls d.Legacy.Update with the same objInfo that was passed to the unified storage call. The previous implementation used an updateWrapper to reuse the already computed updated object. Without it, Legacy.Update will invoke objInfo.UpdatedObject against the legacy store's own old object, which may differ (e.g., missing new fields, different resourceVersion). This can cause the legacy write to produce a different object or fail validation, breaking the dual-write guarantee. The code should pass a wrapper or the object returned by Storage.Update to ensure both stores persist the same data.

findings.title: Multiple metrics are recorded under the wrong name or store
findings.body: Several metric calls are incorrect: in Create error path (line 45) records legacy duration instead of storage; in Update error path (line 129) records legacy duration instead of storage; in Delete success path (line 106) passes the resource name as the 'kind' label instead of options.Kind; in DeleteCollection goroutine (line 166) records storage duration for the legacy operation instead of legacy duration. These errors cause Prometheus metrics to be mislabeled or attributed to the wrong store, leading to incorrect monitoring and alerting. All timing and label arguments must be corrected to reflect the actual operation being measured.

findings.title: Delete uses the base logger instead of the request-scoped logger
findings.body: In Delete, ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) is used, discarding the enriched log variable (log) that includes name, kind, and method fields. Consequently, subsequent logs in the Delete method (including errors from Storage.Delete) will lack these contextual fields, making debugging harder. It should be ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, log).

findings.title: Legacy Create receives the original input object, not the object persisted in unified storage
findings.body: In Create, the goroutine passes `obj` (the original input) to Legacy.Create, ignoring the `created` object returned by Storage.Create. Unified storage typically applies defaulting, assigns UID, resourceVersion, and creationTimestamp. The legacy store will therefore receive an object missing these modifications, leading to data inconsistency between the two stores. The code should pass `created` (or a sanitized copy) to the legacy write to ensure both stores reflect the same final state.

findings.title: Removal of local prometheus registry causes duplicate metric registration panic
findings.body: The diff removes `p := prometheus.NewRegistry()` from TestMode1_Get, causing it to use the package-level global `p` (var p = prometheus.NewRegistry()). If NewDualWriter registers metrics on the provided registry (as dualWriterMetrics likely does using promauto), then the first test that uses the global registry (e.g., TestMode1_Create) will register metrics, and any subsequent test using the same global registry will panic with duplicate metric registration. This will break the entire test package. Each test should create and use its own fresh prometheus registry, or the global registry must be reset between tests.

findings.title: Tests for asynchronous legacy writes do not wait for completion and ignore mock expectations
findings.body: Multiple tests (e.g., TestMode3_Create, TestMode3_Delete, TestMode3_Update) set up legacy mock expectations but never call m.AssertExpectations() and do not wait for the goroutine to finish. The test may pass even if the legacy write is never called or fails, and the mock call may occur after the test completes, causing race conditions or panics if the legacy method is not stubbed. This prevents any verification of the asynchronous dual-write behavior and can lead to flaky or silently failing tests. The tests must synchronize with the goroutine (e.g., using a WaitGroup or a done channel) and assert expectations before finishing.

findings.title: Integration tests for mode 3 may be flaky due to asynchronous legacy writes
findings.body: The added subtests for mode 3 (file and unified storage) run the same doPlaylistTests which immediately checks legacy API results after k8s API operations. Since mode 3 writes to legacy asynchronously, there is no guarantee that the legacy write has completed before the test queries the legacy endpoint. This can cause intermittent failures (e.g., legacy list missing the just-created playlist). The test needs a synchronization mechanism or a polling wait to ensure the async write has propagated before asserting on the legacy API.
